correctness.rationale: One-cycle LF permutation iff last column of a primitive necklace; cyclic input runs equal Hamming(L,sort(L)). Each fully unclustered ternary L of length n is one leaf of 3*2^(n−1) recursive strings. The published parity lemma safely excludes only impossible sharp inputs. The complete C++17 enumeration reproduces all 115 nonzero cells and no others for each n=13..30; independent unpruned computations agree through n24; 115 witnesses separately pass direct inversion and sorting of all cyclic rotations. Known factor-two inequality establishes minimality. The exhaustive finite certificate supports only the finite cutoff.

originality.rationale: The new statement is a complete, exact Parikh-resolved count of all sharp primitive ternary necklaces at every length 13 through 30 (115 nonzero length/type cells), together with all zero cells. The primary 2026 paper states the global bound/conjecture and reports small lengths and selected special families; its full text was inaccessible and this is a documented priority risk. The accessible full CPM 2026 article proves unclustered BWT existence, not counts of minimum-run inputs by individual Parikh vectors. A previously known fixed (m,m,1) slice is explicitly excluded from claims of independent novelty. Neither aggregate existence, a parity restriction, nor the restricted slice implies the complete 18-length census, especially T_14(2,6,6)=0, T_14(4,4,6)=4. The nearest indexed published-finding corpus records do not match the aggregate theorem; absence of search hits is not novelty proof.

value.rationale: This is a motivated exact finite classification for an open BWT run-amplification and Parikh-vector characterization problem, not a relabeling or one-off small computation. It determines all class counts/exclusions for 18 consecutive lengths and 115 realized profiles, surpassing scalar sharpness counts; n14 exhibits a parity-admissible compositional exclusion (2,6,6), revealing genuine structure not implied by previously proved necessary conditions. The cutoff 30 is meaningful as a reproducible benchmark, with no unsupported all-length claim.
